newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent weakens on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent weakens on profit-taking.

text.p: IPE Brent crude oil futures softened on Tuesday in what brokers said was a small correction to Monday's sharp gains.
September Brent was 11 cents a barrel weaker at $19.35 a barrel at 0938 GMT while August gas oil was $3.25 firmer at $175.50 a tonne.
Gas oil was catching up with Brent which put in its strong performance on Monday after the gas oil market closed.
"It is a bit of profit-taking," one broker said. "Yesterday was a bit overdone and it is a reaction to that - there is nothing new out there really."

The U.N. announced on Monday it had reached agreement with Iraq on an aid distribution plan which had been delaying renewed exports and prices, somewhat peversely, rose sharply. Brent ended the day 51 cents firmer on Monday at $19.46.
Brokers said the market strengthened because the Iraqi news was widely anticipated and dealers rushed in to cover short positions when it became clear prices were not going to fall.
Prices were also boosted by strength in the U.S. gasoline markets and more crude oil supply disruptions in Colombia.

"In the very short term the backdrop led by gasoline looks positive, and news that a rebal attack has again caused force majeure on Colombia's Cano Limon field obviously helps," brokers GNI said in a daily report.
But the report added: "During September we expect the ending gasoline season, Iraqi barrels, increased global production and higher inventories to pressure prices."
While dealers expect Iraqi exports to restart in a few working days, once oil contract terms are worked out, uncertainty remains over their expected volume.

Because of delays to the implementation of the oil-for-food deal so far, analyst estimate Iraq may have to export 1.5 to 1.6 million barrels per day to meet a $1 billion cash target by an early September interim deadline.
Oil traders are also awaiting the release overnight of weekly inventory data from the American Petroleum Institute (API.)

"Early predictions are for a 3-4 million barrel crude rise due to the recent refinery problems," GNI said. "This could, along with strong demand, turn into a 2-3 million barrel draw in gasoline stocks and a mild fall in distillate inventories."
Technical analysts said they saw first support for Brent at $19.36 a barrel, and then $19.00-$19.10. Resistance would appear at $19.64 and then around $19.90, they said.
